answer: Graph-conductance cuts resist sybils: a sybil region reaches the honest core only through a thin bundle of edges, forming a low-conductance cut — dense inside, a narrow ridge to cross outward. The system scores clusters by conductance and discounts trust crossing a sparse boundary. Fakes vouching densely among themselves still move only a trickle of trust over that ridge, since weight is bounded by the cut, not internal mass. Honest agents sit in the well-connected harbor of real edges; a farm behind a thin bundle is a relic cluster throttled by its own narrow cut.
